PROJ_NAME: CEDARBURG ALUMINUM DIE CASTING FOUNDRY SUPERFUND SITE
SCOPE: United States Environmental Protection Agency Region 5 (EPA REgion 5) and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) performs Preliminary Design for Aluminum Die Casting Foundry Superfund Site. DETAILS: At former 8.5-acre Aluminum Die Casting Foundry (closed 2005), EPA and USACE will work on the Remedial Design for the site to finalize the technical specifications and cleanup methods. Sampling will take place at the factory site, the natural areas around it and nearby residential properties. Eventually, the EPA will also seek testing on nearby storm sewers and groundwater wells, which are less of a priority, since they're not used for drinking water. The entire site consists of Amcast facility, sewers near the former plant, a stormwater retention pond southeast of Amcast, a pond in nearby Zeunert Park, and some private properties to the southeast. Amcast contaminated the site and surrounding area with polychlorinated biphenyls and other hazardous chemicals. The Amcast site is divided between two properties (Amcast North and Amcast South). The present site of the Amcast South office building was formerly the Meta-Mold Aluminum Company, an aluminum die-cast facility that started operating around 1939. REQUIRES DEMOLITION/RELOCATION/SITE CLEAN UP OF: Finishing/Inspection Equipment, Lighting, Compressors (Air), Hydraulics, Automation/Robotics, Conveyors, Meters, Sensors, Gauges, MCC, Motors, Drives plus Controls (PLC). (A) Ventilation & Exhaust System, Monitors, Ducting; (L) Land/Soil Remediation, Cleanup/Monitoring, Spill Containment; (W) Groundwater & WWTP Monitoring.
SCHEDULE: United States Environmental Protection Agency Region 5 (EPA REgion 5) and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) performs Preliminary Design 2Q25 (May). USACE will be collecting samples and survey data throughout 2025 to help with cleanup design documents and cost estimates. This design will include excavation drawings, pond sediment dredging plans, and other construction documents. The design is expected to be completed in 2026, and the cleanup will start after the design is complete when the rest of the project has been funded. Upon Approvals, EPA REgion 5 and USACE releases Subcontractor Bid Documents as needed 1Q27 (Feb) - 2Q27. Project Kick-Off 3Q27 (Aug). Project Completion 3Q32 (Aug).

PROJ_NAME: CHICAGO STEEL COKE PLANT SUPERFUND SITE CLEANUP/REMEDIATION
SCOPE: United States Environmental Protection Agency Region 5 (EPA Region 5) with Illinois EPA and Cook County Land Bank Authority (Partial Land Owner) performs Preliminary Design for Steel Coke Plant Superfund Site Cleanup/Remediation. ENVIRONMENTAL: Cleanup/Remediate former 104-acre Acme Steel Coke Plant (closed 2001) for productive use to communities. Primary contaminants of concerns at the site are Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs). Large areas of exposed waste are present on-site with elevated levels of PAHs. Additional on-site source areas include a tar pool/impoundment, the facility trench which historically discharged to the nearby Calumet River, and a buried French drain and sump which collected surface and storm water when the plant was in operation. A cleanup could revert the land back to green space and marsh or could include a combination of recreational and commercial development. In 2020 the Cook County Land Bank Authority acquired approximately one-third of the southern part of the former Acme facility, while the northern 61-acre area remains abandoned and in open tax-delinquent status.
